title: Object-oriented design patterns (GoF & kin)
literature: GoF Design Patterns 'Related Patterns' sections; Refactoring.Guru / SourceMaking 'Relations with Other Patterns'; POSA1; Fowler PoEAA; Riehle pattern collaboration.

members.name: Abstract Factory
members.what: An interface for creating families of related or dependent objects without specifying their concrete classes.

members.name: Abstract Session
members.what: A server object hands each client an opaque session object encapsulating the per-client state of their conversation; the client makes further requests through the session rather than the server, with full type safety.

members.name: Acyclic Visitor
members.what: A Visitor variant that breaks the dependency cycle between the element hierarchy and the visitor by using a degenerate base visitor plus per-element visitor interfaces and a runtime cast.

members.name: Adapter
members.what: Converts the interface of a class into another interface clients expect, letting classes with incompatible interfaces work together.

members.name: Bridge
members.what: Decouples an abstraction from its implementation so the two can vary independently, via a handle object delegating to an implementor hierarchy.

members.name: Builder
members.what: Separates the construction of a complex object from its representation so the same construction process can create different representations.

members.name: Bureaucracy
members.what: A compound pattern composing Composite, Mediator, Chain of Responsibility, and Observer to build self-maintaining hierarchical structures where each level mediates its children and escalates requests upward.

members.name: Chain of Responsibility
members.what: Passes a request along a chain of candidate handler objects until one handles it, decoupling sender from receiver.

members.name: Collecting Parameter
members.what: Pass a collecting object through a series of methods, each of which adds its partial results to it, instead of composing return values.

members.name: Command
members.what: Encapsulates a request as an object, letting requests be parameterized, queued, logged, and undone.

members.name: Command Processor
members.what: A dedicated processor component manages user requests reified as command objects: it schedules, executes, logs, and stores them, enabling undo/redo and macro services.

members.name: Component
members.what: Split a single entity's state and behavior across multiple component objects, one per domain (physics, rendering, AI, input), which the entity aggregates.

members.name: Composite
members.what: Composes objects into tree structures representing part-whole hierarchies, letting clients treat individual objects and compositions uniformly.

members.name: Curiously Recurring Template Pattern (CRTP)
members.what: A class derives from a template instantiated with itself, letting the base call derived-class members at compile time.

members.name: Decorator
members.what: Attaches additional responsibilities to an object dynamically by wrapping it in an object with the same interface that forwards and augments requests.

members.name: Delegation
members.what: An object handles a request by forwarding it to a helper object (the delegate), optionally passing itself so the delegate can refer back to the original receiver.

members.name: Domain Service
members.what: A stateless operation in the domain layer, defined by what it does rather than what it is, for domain logic that does not naturally belong to any entity or value object.

members.name: Double Dispatch
members.what: A technique where the operation executed depends on the runtime types of two receivers, implemented by a pair of single dispatches (each object virtual-calls into the other).

members.name: Envelope-Letter
members.what: A handle/body variant where the envelope (handle) and letters (bodies) share a common base class, letting the letter's dynamic type change at runtime behind a stable envelope.

members.name: Extension Object
members.what: Let clients ask an object for an extension implementing a specific interface (getExtension(type)), so new interfaces can be added to a class family without changing its core.

members.name: External Polymorphism
members.what: Make unrelated concrete classes (possibly without virtual functions or a common base) polymorphic by wrapping them in a parallel adapter hierarchy defined outside the classes.

members.name: Facade
members.what: Provides a unified, higher-level interface to a set of interfaces in a subsystem, making the subsystem easier to use.

members.name: Factory Method
members.what: Defines an interface for creating an object but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate, deferring instantiation to subclasses.

members.name: Flyweight
members.what: Uses sharing to support large numbers of fine-grained objects efficiently by factoring state into shared intrinsic and externally supplied extrinsic parts.

members.name: Function Pointer Dispatch Table
members.what: An indexed or keyed table of function pointers replaces switch/if chains: look up the handler, then call it.

members.name: Hook Method
members.what: A method deliberately left empty or with default behavior at a designed extension point, which subclasses or clients override to inject custom behavior into a fixed skeleton.

members.name: Interceptor
members.what: A framework exposes dispatch points where registered interceptor objects are invoked automatically on framework-internal events, letting services be added transparently via callbacks and context objects.

members.name: Interpreter
members.what: Given a language, defines a class per grammar rule and an interpret operation over the resulting abstract syntax tree to evaluate sentences of the language.

members.name: Iterator
members.what: Provides a way to access the elements of an aggregate object sequentially without exposing its underlying representation.

members.name: Layer Supertype
members.what: A common superclass for all types in a layer, holding the behavior every member of that layer shares.

members.name: Mapper
members.what: An object that sets up communication between two independent subsystems that must remain ignorant of each other.

members.name: Marker Interface
members.what: An empty interface whose only purpose is to tag implementing classes with a compile-time-checkable property (Serializable, Cloneable).

members.name: Mediator
members.what: Defines an object that encapsulates how a set of objects interact, so colleagues refer only to the mediator instead of to each other.

members.name: Memento
members.what: Captures and externalizes an object's internal state, without violating encapsulation, so the object can be restored to that state later.

members.name: Mixin
members.what: A small class providing one slice of behavior that is composed into other classes by inheritance (in C++ typically by inheriting from a template parameter) rather than used standalone.

members.name: Monostate
members.what: A class whose every instance shares the same state by declaring all fields static, so construction is unrestricted but behavior is singleton-like.

members.name: Multiton
members.what: A class that manages a map of named instances of itself, guaranteeing exactly one instance per key.

members.name: Non-Virtual Interface (NVI)
members.what: Public interface functions are non-virtual and delegate to private/protected virtual hooks that derived classes override.

members.name: Null Object
members.what: A do-nothing implementation of an interface stands in for 'no object', so clients invoke it uniformly without null checks.

members.name: Object Orientation in C
members.what: Encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism realized in plain C via struct embedding, per-class function-pointer tables, and first-member upcasting.

members.name: Object Recursion
members.what: Distribute the handling of a request recursively over a polymorphic object structure: each recurser handles its part and delegates the remainder to its successor(s) until terminator objects stop the recursion.

members.name: Observer
members.what: Defines a one-to-many dependency between objects so that when one object changes state, all its dependents are notified and updated automatically.

members.name: OO in C via Explicit Vtable
members.what: Structs of function pointers (shared per 'class', pointed to by each instance) plus first-argument self pointers implement classes, inheritance, and dynamic dispatch in C.

members.name: Pluggable Selector
members.what: Store the name (selector) of a method in an instance variable and dispatch on it reflectively, so instances of one class exhibit different behavior without subclassing.

members.name: Policy-Based Design
members.what: Assemble a class's behavior from small orthogonal 'policy' template parameters, each supplying one aspect (allocation, threading, checking).

members.name: Private Class Data
members.what: Move a class's state into a separate data object initialized once at construction, exposing it to the main class only through read access.

members.name: Prototype
members.what: Specifies the kinds of objects to create using a prototypical instance and creates new objects by copying (cloning) this prototype.

members.name: Proxy
members.what: Provides a surrogate or placeholder object that controls access to another object, standing in with the same interface.

members.name: Registry
members.what: A well-known object that other objects use to find common objects and services, typically via static or thread-scoped accessors.

members.name: Role Object
members.what: Adapt a core object to different client contexts by attaching and detaching role objects at runtime, each role extending the core's interface for one context.

members.name: Separated Interface
members.what: Defines an interface in a separate package from its implementation so clients depend only on the interface package.

members.name: Servant
members.what: A helper class that provides a common behavior (e.g., movement, printing) to a group of otherwise unrelated classes, which are passed to the servant as parameters.

members.name: Singleton
members.what: Ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it.

members.name: Special Case
members.what: A subclass that provides special behavior for particular cases (missing customer, unknown value), returned in place of null or an error code.

members.name: Specification
members.what: Encapsulates a business rule as a separate predicate object that can test candidates for satisfaction and be combined with other specifications via and/or/not.

members.name: Sponsor-Selector
members.what: Separate three responsibilities — sponsors that know when a resource is useful, a selector that picks among sponsors' recommendations, and the client that uses the chosen resource — to select the best resource dynamically.

members.name: State
members.what: Lets an object alter its behavior when its internal state changes by delegating state-dependent behavior to interchangeable state objects.

members.name: Strategy
members.what: Defines a family of algorithms, encapsulates each one behind a common interface, and makes them interchangeable within the client that uses them.

members.name: Subclass Sandbox
members.what: A base class defines an abstract sandbox method and a suite of protected operations; subclasses implement their behavior by combining only those provided operations.

members.name: Template Method
members.what: Defines the skeleton of an algorithm in a base-class operation, deferring specific steps to subclass hook methods without changing the algorithm's structure.

members.name: Twin
members.what: Model multiple inheritance in a single-inheritance language by splitting one conceptual object into two closely coupled partner objects, each subclassing one parent and holding a reference to its twin.

members.name: Type Object
members.what: Represent a category of things as an ordinary runtime object (the type object) that instances hold a reference to, instead of as a compile-time class.

members.name: View Handler
members.what: A view handler component manages all views of an application: it opens, coordinates, tiles, clones, updates, and closes them through a uniform view interface.

members.name: Visitor
members.what: Represents an operation to be performed on the elements of an object structure as a separate visitor object, letting new operations be added without changing the element classes (double dispatch).

members.name: Whole-Part
members.what: An aggregate component (the Whole) encapsulates constituent Part objects, organizes their collaboration, and is the sole access point to their combined functionality.
